mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 6.0% and the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 1.0%, the market anticipates a delayed policy response, leading to a temporary equity rally that reverses, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 6.0 and FEDFUNDS < 1.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0), the market prices in a potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is most active in the late phase of the business cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 5.0% for two consecutive months signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to accelerate tightening, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5.0 for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When job growth (PAYEMS) slows (PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% MoM) and industrial production (INDPRO) declines (INDPRO < 100.0), the market anticipates a recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% and INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, leading to wage inflation and potential Fed tightening, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
